why: The criterion holds. I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's six checks and its Advisory. The builder brief has no PASS or FAIL wording. It also reuses none of the verifier's probes: no mktemp/printf scripts, none of its inputs (such as `{bad}`, a.jsonl/ok.jsonl/c.jsonl or missing.jsonl), no git diff/merge-base check and no gh pr checks. Step 3 asks the builder to write its own node:test cases ("two clean files... two `-` arguments... no arguments"), and the rule allows that. Those cases restate the issue's expect lines and include no verifier inputs. Step 5 has the builder run `npm test`, which the issue names. Requirements like "lint(text) must stay byte-for-byte unchanged" and the exit-code rules are targets taken from the expect lines, not commands the verifier runs. So the builder gets the target without the checker's methods.
